This map of Europe's leaders in 1936 can't decide what a leader is. Some names are kings, some presidents, some prime ministers — and in four countries the man who actually held the power isn't on it.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Start with Britain. "Baldwin (Edward VIII)" is a snapshot of a year that had three kings. Edward VIII reigned from 20 January to 11 December 1936, then abdicated over Wallis Simpson after 327 days — the shortest British reign since Lady Jane Grey.

2/ France gives you Lebrun, who was president until 1940 and had little day-to-day power. The man running France from 4 June 1936 was Léon Blum, the Popular Front's first Socialist prime minister, absent from the map entirely.

3/ Poland gives you Mościcki, the president. After Piłsudski died in 1935 his followers split, and Mościcki cut a power-sharing deal that made General Rydz-Śmigły the country's de facto leader. In November 1936 Mościcki made him Marshal of Poland.

4/ Greece gives you George II. In April 1936 the king appointed Ioannis Metaxas prime minister; on 4 August, with the king's signature, Metaxas dissolved parliament, banned parties and suspended the constitution. The dictator isn't named.
5/ Spain gives you Azaña, who became President of the Republic on 10 May 1936. Nine weeks later, on 17–18 July, the generals rose. By the time anyone drew this map Spain had no single leader at all.

6/ The Baltics look like three ordinary republics. All three were already self-coups: Päts declared emergency rule in Estonia in March 1934 and began the Era of Silence, Ulmanis seized power in Latvia that May, Smetona had run Lithuania since 1926.

7/ Switzerland's "Meyer" is the oddest entry. Albert Meyer was President of the Confederation in 1936 — a post that rotates annually among seven federal councillors. Name any other year and Switzerland says someone else.

8/ And one flat error: Belgium is labelled Pierlot. Paul van Zeeland was prime minister throughout 1936, re-forming his national-unity government after the May elections. Pierlot didn't take the job until 1939.

Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
